title: Oven Pulled Pork Sandwiches with Coleslaw
subtitle: pork shoulder slow-roasted until it falls apart, tossed in homemade barbecue sauce and piled on buns with creamy coleslaw
imageAlt: A soft bun piled with saucy pulled pork and creamy coleslaw on a white plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: 8 big sandwiches: dinner for two, plus lunches for days

beforeYouStart.text: This is a weekend recipe: 4 hours in a 150°C (300°F) oven, almost all hands-off.
Use a Dutch oven or a deep roasting pan you can cover tightly with foil.

steps.title: Rub
steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C (300°F). Mix the 2 tbsp brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper and rub all over the pork.

steps.title: Slow-roast
steps.text: Set the pork in the Dutch oven, pour the water around it, cover tightly and roast 3½–4 hours, until a fork twists in with no resistance (about 90–95°C / 195–205°F inside).

steps.title: BBQ sauce
steps.text: Near the end, simmer the ketchup, ⅓ cup brown sugar, 3 tbsp vinegar, Worcestershire and garlic powder in a small pot 5 minutes, until slightly thick.

steps.title: Coleslaw
steps.text: Stir the mayonnaise, 1 tbsp vinegar, sugar and salt together and toss with the coleslaw mix. Chill until serving.

steps.title: Shred
steps.text: Rest the pork 15 minutes, then shred it with 2 forks, discarding any big pieces of fat. Skim the fat off the pan juices and stir ½ cup of the juices and the BBQ sauce into the pork.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile the pork onto the toasted buns and top with coleslaw.

fixIt.fix: It needs more time, not more heat. Cover and roast another 30 minutes, then check again.
Stir in more of the pan juices; shoulder needs the fat and juices to stay moist.
Dress it no more than 2 hours ahead, and drain any liquid before serving.

saleTip: Pork shoulder blade roasts are often under $5/kg at No Frills; it's the cheapest way to feed a crowd.
swap: Slow cooker: rub the pork, add ½ cup water and cook on low 8–9 hours until it shreds.
leftovers: Freeze the pork in its sauce in 2-cup bags; it reheats perfectly for sandwiches, rice bowls or quesadillas.
doneness: Safe at 71°C (160°F) (Health Canada, pork); pulled pork is cooked on to about 90–95°C (195–205°F) so it falls apart. Reheat to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested oven pulled pork methods (Canadian Living, America's Test Kitchen): dry-rubbed shoulder slow-roasted covered at 150°C until shreddable, tossed with a homemade ketchup-based barbecue sauce.
gear: Dutch oven or roasting pan with foil
prepAhead: Rub the pork the night before and keep it covered in the fridge.
Make the BBQ sauce up to 1 week ahead.
The cooked pork keeps 4 days and reheats well.
reheat: Covered over medium-low with a splash of water, stirring, or in the microwave 2 minutes, stirring halfway, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Salt, pepper, paprika and brown sugar on the pork, and the sauce from ketchup and brown sugar; no coleslaw.

stepNotes.0: Basic: brown sugar, paprika, salt and pepper.
stepNotes.2: Basic: ketchup, brown sugar and vinegar only.

fancy.note: Melted cheddar on the pork and sweet pickles on top.

stepNotes.5: Fancy: top the pork on the bottom buns with cheddar and broil 1 minute to melt, then add pickles and coleslaw.

plating: Coleslaw on top, not on the side.
Extra sauce in a small jug.

why.0-0: Shoulder has lots of fat and connective tissue that melt in a long, low roast, so it shreds and stays juicy.
why.1-2: Vinegar balances the sweet, rich pork and is the classic barbecue sauce tang.
why.2-0: Cool, crunchy coleslaw cuts through the rich pork.

funFact: Pulled pork comes from the Carolinas, where whole hogs were slow-smoked for hours and pulled apart by hand.

keeps.note: freeze the pork in its sauce; coleslaw doesn't freeze
